page: Vultr voc-m-16c-128gb-1600s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs and 128.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor running at 2.0 GHz, the system features 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The hardware profile includes 1600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a single complimentary public IPv4 address, with no integrated GPU.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory performance, with a PassMark memory score in the top 25% and uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaching 131.64 GB/sec. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is highly competitive, placing in the top 10% with a score of 3207.88, while multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores align with the middle 50% average. For lightweight machine learning tasks, the server demonstrates strong text generation speeds of 263.35 tokens/sec using a small 135M parameter model, though larger models or multi-threaded decompression tasks perform at average tier levels.

Given its 8.0 GB of RAM per core and dedicated CPU allocation, this instance offers a balanced resource density for memory-intensive workloads without the premium of GPU-accelerated hardware. The combination of 1600 GB local NVMe storage and high memory capacity makes it well-suited for database hosting, memory-cached web serving, and moderate data processing pipelines.
